source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. CPU Common Options → SMU and PSP Debug Mode: Disabled e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Correctable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --smupsp --socket 0 --errormode 3 --enablemcapolling 0 --errorindex 0 --errortype 0 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- MPIO Correctable Error: inject the MPIO MPIO Correctable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'smu|mp1|mp5|mpio|firmware.error|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __MPIO_MPIO_Correctable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.test_name: MPIO Correctable Error — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Inject one correctable error in the platform-defined MPIO block, verify an exact fresh corrected report without reset or UCE escalation, and demonstrate that every MPIO-owned interface and dependent service remains functional.
required_package: Authoritative expansion/definition of MPIO and its firmware block, interfaces and service dependencies
Vendor semantics for smupsp errormode3, enablemcapolling0, errorindex0 and errortype0
Socket/package coverage and whether index0 maps to one or multiple interfaces
FFE threshold and SMU/PSP-debug-disable relevance with raw restore values
Fresh MPIO-specific CE source/severity/count plus explicit no-reset/no-UCE oracle
Supported OS, timeout, interface transaction and service-health limits, aborts and restoration
test_case.test_command: Obtain the vendor MPIO definition and interface ownership map; validate mode3/index0/socket coverage; capture raw settings, counters and service baselines; inject once; correlate exactly one MPIO-specific CE; check no reset/UCE; exercise only approved non-destructive interface transactions; restore RAS/HDT state and compare health.
test_case.expected_result: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.

safety_gate: Dedicated SUT with independent OOB access not dependent on the interface under test
Baseline all MPIO-owned interface links, counters and services before injection
Use a non-destructive isolated transaction for health checking and inject once
Abort on reset, UCE, management-path loss, interface link/counter anomaly, service failure or wrong source
No automatic retry; restore settings and confirm all dependent paths return to baseline
expected_evidence: Vendor MPIO block/interface/service map and approved tuple semantics
Raw BIOS/HDT, error-counter, interface and service baseline
Exact injection transcript and no-reset timeline
Exactly one fresh MPIO-specific CE MCA/CPER/WHEA/SEL record with zero UCE delta
Stable interface links/counters, isolated transactions and dependent services
test_case.recovery: If MPIO controls the only management path, establish an independent recovery channel before execution. Do not equate MPIO with Linux multipath I/O or another familiar acronym without the vendor specification.
